correctness.rationale: The real zero-sum metric dual is exactly the intersection of within-class slabs of width t and cross-class slabs of width 1; H decomposes orthogonally as A-zero-sum, B-zero-sum, and the one-dimensional class contrast. Uniqueness and origin symmetry of the full-dimensional John ellipsoid, then S_p×S_q invariance, force shape aP_A+bP_B+cP_C without restricting an arbitrary competitor. For any pair difference the squared support is 2a (A), 2b (B), or αa+βb+γc (cross), with α=(p−1)/p, β=(q−1)/q, γ=(p+q)/(pq). The log determinant (p−1)ln(a)+(q−1)ln(b)+ln(c) is strictly concave under a,b≤T=t²/2 and αa+βb+γc≤1; solving exact KKT produces the stated branches at T1=q/(2q−1), T2=q/(p+q−1), including p=q merger. Strict positivity, multiplier signs, support equalities, and complementarity make the branches globally optimal. The cross support always equals 1, and a=T/b=T characterize contacts. At and after T2 the shape freezes although a chosen within-A potential with gap t<t′≤2 witnesses strict enlargement of Q; saturation t*=sqrt(2q/(p+q−1)) is sharp. An independently written NumPy/Python checker tested 518 p,q,T triples across all branches and boundaries and independently recomputed KKT feasibility/signs/complementarity; arithmetic floats are corroboration, not an infinite proof.
